Confidence sets for functional intraclass correlation coefficient, ICC, in Test-Retest Reliability

Conf_sets.Rd

This function calculates the confidence sets for functional ICC in Test-Retest setting. All Confidence sets explained in Seydi MR, Pini A, Pataky TC, Schelin L. Confidence sets for intraclass correlation coefficients in test–retest curve measurements. Journal of Biomechanics. 2024 Aug 1;173:112232. Note that pointwise F bands do not provide simultaneous coverage. Furthermore, this confidence bands have not investigated for unbalanced cases so far.

Usage

Conf_sets(
  test,
  retest,
  individuals = NULL,
  type = c("Rank", "Normal"),
  n_boot = 1000,
  designation = "ICC(A,1)",
  alpha = 0.05,
  resample_trials = FALSE
)

Arguments

test

A matrix of test measurements with rows representing individuals and columns representing evaluation points.

retest

A matrix of retest measurements with rows representing individuals and columns representing evaluation points.

individuals

A vector of individual identifiers. It must be the combined vector of individual identifiers for test and retest. If NULL, the function assumes that the individuals in the test and retest matrices are the same.

type

A character vector specifying the type of confidence sets to be calculated. Possible values are "Rank" for ICC curve confidence bands, and "Normal" for integrated ICC confidence interval. The user can choose one or both. The default value is both "Rank" and "Normal".

n_boot

A numeric value specifying the number of bootstrap samples. The default value is 1000.

resample_trials

Logical; whether to resample trial rows within each selected individual and session during bootstrapping. Defaults to FALSE, which resamples individuals but keeps their observed trials unchanged.

designation

A character string specifying the designation of the ICC. Possible values are "ICC(A,1)" and "ICC(A,k)". Possible designation is "ICC(A,1)", "ICC(A,k)" based on the paper: McGraw KO, Wong SP. Forming inferences about some intraclass correlation coefficients. Psychological methods. 1996 Mar;1(1):30. The default value is "ICC(A,1)".

alpha

A numeric value specifying the significance level for the ICC calculation. The default value is 0.05.

Value

A list containing the pointwise ICC values, integrated ICC value, and the confidence sets.

Examples

# The package contains the datasets, TEST_data, and RETEST_data which are the
#test and retest data, respectively.


set.seed(123)
confsets_outputs <- Conf_sets(test = TEST_data, retest = RETEST_data,
                             type = c("Rank", "Normal"), n_boot=1000,
                             designation = "ICC(A,1)", alpha = 0.05,
                             resample_trials = FALSE)

#Consider the scenario with unbalanced case, in total we have 28 individuals,
#and for example the individuals number 2 has attended 1 test and 2 retest trials,
#number 3 has attended 3 test and 2 retest trials,
#the other individuals have attended only one trials.
#Then the individuals vector should be like
# c(1:2, rep(3, 3), 4:28, 1, rep(2,2), rep(3, 2), 4:28).

set.seed(1234)
confsets_outputs <- Conf_sets(test = TEST_data, retest = RETEST_data,
                             individuals = c(1:2, rep(3, 3), 4:28, 1, rep(2,2),
                             rep(3, 2), 4:28),
                             type = c("Rank", "Normal"), n_boot=1000,
                             designation = "ICC(A,1)", alpha = 0.05,
                             resample_trials = FALSE)
